name: go-gobra-bench
description: Code and benchmark accompanying the anonymous submission "How Far Are LLMs from Verifying Go? An Empirical Study of Specification and Proof Synthesis with Gobra". The study investigates specification and proof synthesis for fixed Go programs using Gobra across three paradigms: single-shot generation (Direct), tool-using synthesis (Agent/OpenCode), and a verifier-feedback workflow (AutoGobra). The go-gobra-bench.zip archive contains 349 tasks, including natural-language requirements, target programs, reference solutions, required dependencies, verification configurations, feature labels, and source attribution. SOURCE-CLUSTERS.csv groups the tasks by 191 source programs for cluster-based analysis. The autogobra-code.zip archive contains implementations of the three paradigms, operator prompts, independent acceptance checks, LLM-judge tools for requirement faithfulness and program-boundary preservation, ablation variants, dependency declarations, example configurations, and instructions for running the experiments. Experiment results and frozen run archives are not included. Reproduction requires a separately installed verifier and user-supplied model service. Private endpoints and credentials have been replaced with placeholders or environment-variable references. See the included README for prerequisites, commands, and limitations.
